title: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
aka: the three young men in the furnace
lead: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah were Jewish young men of Judah taken to Babylon with Daniel and renamed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. They refused to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue and were thrown into a furnace and rescued (Daniel 3). The Greek Daniel adds their prayer and hymn inside the furnace.

sections.h: In the Hebrew and Aramaic book
sections.b: They share Daniel's training and refusal of the king's food (Daniel 1), pray with him for mercy over the king's dream (2:17-18), are put over the province of Babylon at his request (2:49), and refuse to worship the statue (3:12). Their answer, "and if he does not" (3:18), is the center of the story. They are not mentioned after chapter 3.

1 Maccabees 2:59-60 names them among those saved by faith; First Clement 45:6-7 and 4 Maccabees 16:21 use them as examples of endurance; the Talmud (Pesachim 53b) makes them models of sanctifying God's name. Hebrews 11:34 refers to those who quenched the power of fire. The Greek Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three, called the Benedicite, are used in Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican worship.
